bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is copied into the static global request buffer `data_copy[32767]` and fills it completely: bytes 0..8 are `PROX\r\n   `, and bytes 9..32766 contain no further space byte and no NUL terminator. Because proxy parsing is enabled, `parse_http_request()` dispatches on the first four bytes `PROX` into `parse_proxy_protocol_v1()`. That parser finds the first `\r` at offset 4 and accepts the six-byte line `PROX\r\n`, but still assumes the input starts with `"PROXY "` and sets `protocol = buffer + 6`, which already points two bytes past the parsed line end. Vulnerable `strsep_char()` then tokenizes from that out-of-line pointer with unbounded `strchr`. The first three calls consume the three spaces at offsets 6, 7, and 8 even though they are beyond the recorded line end, advancing the cursor to `src_port = data_copy + 9`. The fourth call searches for another space from that position; because the exact witness contains no in-bounds space or NUL after offset 8, `strchr` scans through the rest of global `data_copy` and into the redzone. AddressSanitizer reports `global-buffer-overflow READ of size 32759` at `strsep_char` line 148. The fix adds an `end` argument and rejects delimiters found past the recorded line end with `if (UNLIKELY(ptr > end)) return NULL;`, so the very first out-of-line split fails instead of advancing to the crashing search.

source.description: First non-harness parser step on the vulnerable path that reads the attacker-controlled request bytes, locates the CRLF terminating the purported PROXY v1 line, and materializes the line boundary later violated by tokenization.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is exactly 32767 bytes long. Its first nine bytes are `50 52 4f 58 0d 0a 20 20 20` (`PROX\r\n   `), so after `parse_proxy_protocol()` dispatches on the four-byte `PROX` prefix this step finds `end = data_copy + 4`, verifies `end[1] == '\n'`, and records `size = 6`.

root_cause.description: The token splitter uses unbounded `strchr` and blindly returns `ptr + 1` without checking whether the found delimiter is still within the caller's recorded line extent. On the first split of the malformed proxy line, it accepts the space at `data_copy + 6` even though the line ended at `data_copy + 4`.
root_cause.note: The fix changes this exact obligation by passing `end` into `strsep_char()` and adding `if (UNLIKELY(ptr > end)) return NULL;` before mutating the delimiter and returning the next cursor.

sink.description: ASan sink. The fourth `strsep_char()` call searches for another space from `src_port = data_copy + 9`, but the exact 32767-byte witness contains no in-bounds space or NUL after that point, so `strchr` reads off the end of global `data_copy`.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow READ of size 32759` at `src/lib/lwan-request.c:148:11` and says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of global `data_copy` defined in `fuzz_parse_http_request` line 1650.

tainted_value_origin.description: Materializes the exact staged witness in the static global array later named by ASan. In the saved run `length` is 32767, so every byte of `data_copy` is overwritten by attacker-controlled input and there is no in-bounds trailing NUL left in the buffer.
tainted_value_origin.note: Direct inspection of the staged `poc` shows bytes 0..8 are `PROX\r\n   `, there are exactly three space bytes total, and there is no `0x00` byte anywhere in the 32767-byte file.

parser_admitted.description: With `REQUEST_ALLOW_PROXY_REQS` set by the fuzz harness, the witness's first four bytes are `PROX`, so `parse_http_request()` enters the PROXY v1 parser even though the line is only `PROX\r\n` rather than a valid `PROXY ` header.

coarse_trace.summary: The fuzz harness copies the 32767-byte witness into static global `data_copy`, publishes the full logical span as `helper->buffer`, enables proxy parsing, and calls `parse_http_request()`.
The request parser dispatches on the four-byte prefix `PROX`, accepts `PROX\r\n` as a terminated proxy line, and then derives `protocol = buffer + 6`, which already points beyond that line end.

Three successive `strsep_char()` calls treat the out-of-line spaces at offsets 6..8 as valid field separators, advancing to `src_port = data_copy + 9`; the fourth `strchr` search for another space then runs across the rest of global `data_copy` and triggers the saved ASan global-buffer-overflow.

fine_trace.note: Copies the exact staged witness into the static global array later named by ASan. In this run `length` is 32767, so the copy fills `data_copy[0..32766]` completely. The exact file begins `PROX\r\n   `, contains exactly three space bytes at offsets 6, 7, and 8, and contains no in-bounds NUL byte anywhere.
Publishes the copied bytes to the request parser as the logical buffer `[data_copy, data_copy + 32767)`. Later pointer arithmetic and the saved ASan global name are both relative to this span.

Source. After `parse_proxy_protocol()` dispatches on the witness's four-byte `PROX` prefix, this step finds the first `\r` at offset 4, verifies the following `\n`, stores `end = data_copy + 4`, writes a terminator there, and records the parsed proxy-line size as 6 bytes.

Derives the start of the would-be protocol token by assuming the buffer begins with `"PROXY "`. On the staged witness this yields `protocol = data_copy + 6`, which is already two bytes past `end = data_copy + 4` and points at the first space after the accepted `PROX\r\n` line.

Root cause. The first call from `src_addr = strsep_char(protocol, ' ')` enters with `strp = protocol = data_copy + 6`. `strchr` immediately finds the space at offset 6, overwrites it with `\0`, and returns `src_addr = data_copy + 7` even though that delimiter lies past `end = data_copy + 4`. There is no `ptr > end` check to reject this out-of-line split.

The second split repeats the same pattern on the next out-of-line space. With `src_addr = data_copy + 7`, `strsep_char()` consumes the space at offset 7 and returns `dst_addr = data_copy + 8` instead of rejecting a delimiter beyond `end`.
The third split consumes the last out-of-line space at offset 8 and returns `src_port = data_copy + 9`, which points at the first non-space byte (`0xff`) after the CRLF and three spaces.

Sink. The fourth call from `dst_port = strsep_char(src_port, ' ')` enters with `strp = src_port = data_copy + 9`. Step 0 established that the exact 32767-byte witness contains no further space byte and no NUL terminator after offset 8, so this unbounded `strchr` search walks through the remaining bytes of `data_copy` and one byte into the global redzone. The saved sanitizer trace reports `global-buffer-overflow READ of size 32759` at this line.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the invalid read is 0 bytes to the right of global variable `data_copy` defined here with size 32767.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run on `gt_results/arvo_14509/poc` reproduced `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow READ of size 32759 in strsep_char`, with `parse_proxy_protocol_v1 -> parse_http_request` immediately below it in the stack.

format.name: malformed PROXY v1 request prefix
format.contract: Exactly the 32767-byte witness stored in `poc`. Bytes 0..8 are `50 52 4f 58 0d 0a 20 20 20` (`PROX\r\n   `). Bytes 9..32766 contain no `0x20` space byte and no `0x00` NUL byte, so the copied request fills `data_copy[32767]` completely without an in-bounds terminator. The first four bytes select `parse_proxy_protocol_v1()`, the first CRLF ends the accepted line at offset 4, and the three spaces at offsets 6..8 advance tokenization to the final unbounded `strchr(src_port, ' ')` search.
